title: Residency Request Decision Ladder and Intake Template for Region Availability
creator: Ava Liang
description: Decision ladder and standard intake for handling customer requests about region availability, data residency constraints, and failover requirements. This ticket captures an operational rubric ("decision ladder"), an intake form template for CS/AE to use, and a scoring model to prioritize requests across Hosted, Dedicated and Private offerings.
background: We receive frequent enterprise asks to: (1) enable a new cloud region, (2) provide data residency guarantees for specific countries, or (3) add failover regions with contractual SLAs. Current intake is ad hoc — requests live in email/Slack and decisions are inconsistent. We need a deterministic, repeatable process that balances customer needs, legal/regulatory constraints, and infra cost/complexity.
goals: (1) Provide a one-page intake form for sales/CS to submit requests with essential signals. (2) Define a decision ladder that routes requests to the right path: Auto-approve for low-cost infra replication, Review for compliance cases, Escalate for new-region builds. (3) Create a transparent scoring rubric to prioritize backlog and communicate timelines to customers.
scope_included: New region activation requests, explicit data residency (in-region storage) requirements, failover region requests tied to contractual SLAs, requests from enterprise customers or >$50k ARR prospects.
scope_excluded: Ad-hoc performance complaints (use infra reliability tickets), requests for improved observability dashboards (product tickets), or non-regulatory localization features (language support).
intake_form_template:
- Customer name/company
- Customer tier (Self-serve / Growth / Enterprise)
- Product mode required (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Requested region(s) or residency country
- Regulatory reason (GDPR, Schrems II, APPI, HIPAA, Other - specify)
- Data types (PII, health, financial, non-sensitive)
- Desired SLA/Failover RTO and RPO
- Commercial ask (contract clause, warranty, penalty)
- Timeline / go-live date
- Contact (AE/CS owner)
- Attachments (contract excerpts, legal memos, compliance attestations)
scoring_criteria:
Scores are additive; higher score = higher priority. Components:
- Revenue signal: ARR or pipeline size (0-30)
- Regulatory risk (0-30): regulatory mandate or legal prohibition increases score
- Engineering complexity (0-20): existing infra support vs new infra build
- Operational risk (0-10): ongoing ops burden (monitoring, backups)
- Strategic value (0-10): referenceability, market entry importance
Thresholds: >=60 -> High priority (target 8-12 week engineering sprint); 35-59 -> Medium (consider in upcoming allocation or Dedicated roadmap); <35 -> Low (queue into backlog, offer workaround guidance)
triage_workflow:
1) Sales/CS submits intake form into the PRD intake GSheet and links to ticket.
2) PM Triage (weekly): review new requests, apply scoring criteria, and assign preliminary priority.
3) Compliance/Legal quick-check (48h): if regulatory risk >15, Legal reviews and flags controls needed.
4) Architecture review (5 business days) if engineering complexity >10 or new region required.
5) Decision: Auto-approve + implementation (low complexity), Plan + schedule (medium), Executive escalation (high).
6) Communicate decision and expected timeline back to AE/CS.
decision_rubric_examples: Example A: Enterprise customer ($500k ARR) requests EU-only residency for PII tied to contract clause -> revenue signal 25 + regulatory risk 25 + complexity 10 + ops 5 + strategic 8 = 73 (High). Example B: SMB customer asks for Singapore region without legal mandate -> revenue 5 + regulatory 5 + complexity 8 + ops 2 + strategic 1 = 21 (Low).
success_metrics:
- Time from intake to decision (target <10 business days for non-escalated items)
- Percentage of residency requests with an assigned timeline (target 90%)
- Conversion of high-priority requests to signed contracts or product commits within 3 months (target 60%)
- Reduced ad-hoc Slack threads about region decisions (qualitative)
rollout_recommendations: Pilot the intake + decision ladder with three AE/CS teams for 6 weeks. Instrument a lightweight GSheet + webhook to Linear to create standardized tickets. After pilot, fold intake into Console support portal as a form and link to PM triage board. Publish a short SLA matrix for customers (expected timeline by priority band).
notes_and_risks:
- Some legal reviews may require customer-provided documentation which slows timelines.
- New region builds have non-linear cost; scoring must reflect recurring infra ops.
- Dedicated and Private customers might need separate legal/commercial pathways (handled as routing rule in intake).
- Risk of over-promising timelines on medium-priority items; recommend conservative public timelines.
